## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppādavāra* (Ya 4.2.1) is a structural section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. In the overall compositional schema of the *Yamaka*, doctrinal concepts across various chapters are analyzed dynamically through process sections (*pavattivāra*), which are systematically divided into origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and origination-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007; Ronkin 2005]. Within the *uppādavāra*, questions explore origination across temporal dimensions (present, past, and future) and analytical standpoints—specifically in relation to person (*puggala*), realm or plane (*okāsa*), and both person and realm (*puggala-okāsa*), framed in both positive and negative formulations [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Modern scholars note that this process-oriented treatment reflects early Buddhist process metaphysics and constitutes an important transitional milestone toward the classical Abhidhamma theory of momentariness, introducing the subdivision of a temporal moment into sub-moments of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and dissolution (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Ronkin 2005].
